direction: Refine the offline `score_item` priority to break the 2-3% gap on the small/medium instances: prioritize large items (size descending) but perturb ties with a deterministic hashed jitter so that FFD-like packing explores alternative insertion orders, and let the repack pass relocate the smallest items of under-filled bins. Push toward reducing bin count on size=50 (13.0 mean) and size=100 (24.25 mean) regimes.

operations.mechanism: Round 1 produced a single solver at mean objective 28.1667 with zero VBS gap, so the only available signal is the per-size relative gap reported in archive feedback (size 50: 2.72%, size 100: 2.41%, size 200: 1.52%). KB search returned no entries for offline BPP priority heuristics in this release, so the plan is driven by the archive's weakest-regime evidence rather than literature. The dominant failure mode in decreasing-order bin packing is tie ambiguity among equal/large items, which changes whether the tail of small items fits into existing bins; adding a bounded deterministic secondary term to `score_item` is a low-risk, sub-millisecond change well inside the 500 ms budget and keeps postprocess `none` so the improvement is attributable to ordering alone.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: If `score_item` is a lexicographic priority: (a) size descending as the base term, plus (b) a bounded deterministic tie-break term derived from a cheap residual-fit heuristic (e.g. item size modulo the dominant bin-fill quantum, or hash(size) so equal-size items are ordered consistently yet differently across bins), then the reorder-repack loop will close part of the ~2.4-2.7% relative gap on size 50/100 instances without regressing size 200, because FFD orderings tie on large items and the residual term drives the small-item placement that determines whether the last bin is needed.
